description: We are a team of Data Science and Mathematics Engineering students from Tecnológico de Monterrey, interested in applying artificial intelligence, statistics, mathematical modeling, and data visualization to real-world scientific problems.
summary: AETHER-SI is an interactive, AI-assisted dashboard that helps engineers, researchers and students find, compare and interpret NASA's microgravity combustion research for crewed exploration. It combines live records from NASA's PSI Data Repository with technical literature from the NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS) and organizes them into a common data model: fuel, oxygen concentration, pressure, flow, hardware and safety pillar (prevention, detection, suppression). Users can rank evidence by mission scenario (ISS/Gateway, Artemis lunar base, lunar rover, EVA suit), compare two runs side by side to see which conditions changed, and ask for an AI-written interpretation whose numbers are checked against the source data. A PSI-Nexus graph shows how experiments relate, and a Student mode explains the same evidence in plain language. Numeric values come only from NASA tables and reports with citations, and anything not reported is shown as missing, never estimated.
details:
What it does

NASA has studied flames in microgravity for decades, but results are scattered across dozens of investigations. AETHER-SI lets users explore them in one place:

- Catalog: 15 curated studies and 23 normalized experimental runs (BASS-II, Saffire, SAME, SAME-R, FLEX and others), each run citing the table or section of the NASA report it came from. Additional Combustion Science investigations are pulled live from NASA PSI, with a versioned snapshot as a fallback if the service is unavailable. Studies without quantitative data appear as reference cards.

- Scenario ranking (FSRS): evidence is ranked by similarity to a mission profile (ISS/Gateway, Artemis lunar base, lunar rover, EVA suit, terrestrial mining), or to custom gravity, oxygen, pressure and flow values. Each score shows its breakdown and flags when a value is only a bound.

Scenario coverage: for the active scenario, the dashboard shows the closest measured run, the gap in each variable, and how many runs fall within tolerance.

AI interpretation: the "Interpret" button writes a plain-language reading of a comparison or ranking using Google Gemini. Every number in the response is validated against the underlying data on the server; if the model is unavailable or the check fails, a rule-based summary is shown instead.

- Evidence assistant: answers questions about a study, a run or the active comparison, with links to sources.

- Search: local concept and synonym search in Spanish and English.

- PSI-Nexus graph: relationships between facilities, studies, topics and runs, with views for conditions and A/B schema.

- A/B comparator: shows what changed between two runs as a table, charts or matrix, with sources, and warns when several conditions changed at once so a difference is not attributed to a single variable.

- Experiment scene: a view of the setup for supported runs

- Student mode: adds explanations to the same evidence.

Benefits and intended impact

It helps engineers and researchers quickly find the evidence most relevant to habitats with ≥30% O₂ at ≤10.2 psi, and gives modelers clean, cited data. It supports prevention, detection and suppression. It also makes the evidence gaps visible, and Student mode opens the same material to learners.

Data integrity

Numeric values come only from NASA tables and reports, with citations. Missing values are shown as missing and are never estimated. Where a study reports only a nominal value (e.g., O₂ in SAME), the dashboard marks it and states the basis. AI-generated text cannot introduce numbers that are not in the data. The dashboard declares that PSI has no partial-gravity data (expected from LUCI and FM2); microgravity and 1 g are shown as bounds.

Tools and technologies

Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, zustand, @xyflow/react, lucide-react, Vitest, Google Gemini API, deployed on Vercel. Data from the NASA PSI Data Repository (CC0) and the NASA Technical Reports Server, cited by DOI or report number.
